questions: Have you been taking any medications regularly, especially anti-psychotics or metoclopramide (for nausea), in the last year?
Do you have a family history of Huntington's disease or similar movement disorders?
Did these movements begin abruptly (over minutes or hours)?
Are you experiencing any memory loss, confusion, or changes in your personality?

results: 1. action specificity and task dependence: dystonia appears on INITIATING SPEECH; asymptomatic at rest
2. medication and toxin exposure history: methotrexate 15 mg weekly for six years for psoriatic arthritis; the dystonia improved after switching to sulfasalazine
3. dystonia rating scale (BFM / OMDRS): Oromandibular Dystonia Rating Scale 177 at baseline, 103 three months after the drug switch, 75 after adding botulinum toxin
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Methotrexate-induced oromandibular dystonia
Idiopathic (cryptogenic) oromandibular dystonia
Tardive dystonia secondary to an undisclosed dopamine receptor blocking agent (e.g., metoclopramide or an antipsychotic)
Symptomatic focal dystonia secondary to a structural lesion of the basal ganglia (e.g., stroke or tumor)
